The appellant contends that this land is double crop wet lands irrigated by a Minor Irrigation Tank and bore wells.

3. Aggrieved by the said acquisition process initiated,
by notification, dated 21.03.2006, the appellant had approached the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh, by way of W.P.No.4159 of 2008.
A learned Single Judge of the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh, on 28.02.2008, granted an interim order of status quo pending further orders.
The interim order is in force, as the Writ Petition has not been disposed of.

4. While the Writ Petition is pending, the District Collector had issued a notification, dated 15.12.2024, under Section 11(1) of Act 30 of 2013 proposing to acquire various extents of land,
including the land of the appellant for the public purpose of establishing an Industrial Corridor/Special Economic Zone.
Subsequently, a declaration under Section 19(1) was published, by the district collector, on 25.02.2025.
This notification was challenged by the appellant, by way of W.P.No.5833 of 2025.

In this Writ Petition, the appellant sought an interim direction, by RRR,J &
Dr. KMR,J way of I.A.No.1 of 2025, for stay of all further proceedings pursuant to the notification,
dated 15.12.2024 and declaration, dated 25.02.2025.
5.
The appellant raised various grounds in support of his contention as to why the acquisition process cannot be taken forward.
It appears that similar Writ Petitions and similar applications have been moved by three other affected persons.
6. A learned Single Judge of this Court, by way of a common order, dated 24.03.2025, passed in the applications filed in all the three Writ Petitions had rejected the applications.
Aggrieved by the order of rejection in I.A.No.1 of 2025 in W.P. No.5833 if 2025, the appellant has approached this Court.

7. The case of the appellant, as recorded by the learned Single Judge, was that the 2nd respondent-District Collector did not have jurisdiction to issue the notification, dated 15.12.2024, or the declaration, dated 25.02.2025.
The petitioner contended that such a notification and declaration could have been issued only by the 1st respondent, who answers the description of appropriate government'.
The 2nd respondent cannot be treated to be appropriate government' inasmuch as no notification, under the proviso to Section 3(e) of Act 30 of 2013, had been RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J issued.
Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Dinesh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh.1 8.

The division bench has also held that, this interpretation was available on a conjoint reading of Section 3(e) with Section 109(1) and Section 112 of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013.

10. The learned Single Judge accepted the submissions of the learned Government Pleader and had rejected the application of the appellant, on the ground that the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court was not applicable as there was no provision, akin to Rule 2 (b) of the Andhra Pradesh Rules,
in the Madhya Pradesh Rules.

11. Sri D. Krishna Murthy, learned counsel appearing for Sri V. Vinod K. Reddy, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the learned Single Judge had erred in dismissing the application despite the fact that an order of status quo, granted earlier in W.P.No.41519 of 2008 on 28.02.2008 was still in subsistence.

The learned counsel would also submit that the law laid down by the Division Bench in W.P.No.32956 of 2015, requires reconsideration, as the publication of a Rule,
which includes the District Collector, within the definition of appropriate RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J government', under Rule 2(b) would not meet the requirement of notification under the proviso to Section 3(e) of the Act.
12. The learned Advocate General appearing for the respondents submits that the earlier acquisition process had been challenged by various other land losers resulting in a batch of cases.

The learned Advocate General would submit that the order of the learned Single Judge dated 28.02.2008, on which reliance is placed by the appellant, itself states that the Writ Petition was to be posted along with W.P.No.51713 of 2007 and batch.
The learned Advocate General would submit that the said batch had been disposed of, as the State had informed the Court that the proposed acquisition of lands had been given up.

The learned Advocate General would submit that in such circumstances,
the order of status quo, dated 28.02.2008, in W.P.No.41519 of 2008 would not be applicable to the present case as the acquisition process, under challenge in the present Writ Petition, is completely different from the acquisition process which was under challenge in W.P.No.41519 of 2008.

Apart from this, the learned Advocate General would contend that W.P.No.41519 of 2008, which was not attached to W.P.No.51713 of 2007 and batch, could not be disposed of as the said Writ petition had escaped the attention of everybody.
He would submit that in such circumstances, the order of status quo granted RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J in W.P.No.41519 of 2008 cannot be a ground for stalling the present acquisition process.

13. The learned Advocate General would also contend that the present acquisition process, for an extent of 17  acres approximately, was part of the process of acquiring land for the establishment P. He would submit that in such circumstances, it would only be appropriate to allow the acquisition process to go on.

14. Sri D. Krishna Murthy, learned counsel for the appellant contends that the order granted in W.P.No.41519 of 2008 would apply to the present situation also as the acquisition, which was under challenge in W.P.No.41519 of 2008, was for establishment of SEZ and the acquisition, in the present case is also for establishment of SEZ.
15.

The learned counsel would also contend that, under the provisions of Section 21 of the Act, a minimum period of 30 days have to be granted from the date of publication of the notification,
under Section 21, before the award proceedings can be completed.

In the present case, RRR,J & Dr.
KMR,J the declaration was issued on 25.02.2025 whereas the State claims that an award had been passed, much before the expiry of 30 days from the said date and consequently, the award itself is invalid.

The learned Advocate General has stated that he would look into this question and that the acquisition authority, would disregard the award if it has been passed before the time set out under the Act and a fresh award would be passed.

Consideration of the Court:
16.
The appellant had challenged the acquisition proceedings of 2006, which had been initiated for establishing a Special Economic Zone.

A learned Single Judge of the erstwhile High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh, had granted status quo existing on the day of the order to be maintained.

sentences.text: While there is no dispute that writ petitions filed against the same acquisition process had been disposed of, the fact remains that the present Writ Petition has not been disposed of and the order of the learned Single Judge continues to hold the field.

17. The State, instead of getting the said writ petition closed, on the ground that the notification under challenge had lapsed, has chosen to take the stand that the said order of status quo does not preclude further acquisition process.
We are unable to accept this contention.
RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J

Though the order of the learned Single Judge was passed in the context of the acquisition process, initiated under the notification, dated 21.03.2006, the same would enure to the benefit of the petitioner, in relation to any further acquisition of the land, for the same purpose.

18. Before going into the contention of the appellant that the notification and declaration apart from the exemption notification, issued by the District Collector are without jurisdiction, it would be necessary to notice a few provisions of the 2013 Act.

Rule 2(b) of the Andhra Pradesh Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Rules, 2014:
2(b) Appropriate Government means the State Government and includes the District Collector of the concerned District for any extent of land to be acquired for a public purpose within the jurisdiction of the revenue district.
RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J 19.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Rules, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The scheme of the Act requires that, where any land is sought to be acquired, the appropriate government would have to carry through a process of consultation and investigation for determining the social impact that would occur on account of the acquisition of the land and whether the public purpose is sufficient to overcome such social impact.
The provisions of Section 4 to Section 10, set out the manner in which such impact assessment is to be carried out and the effect of the findings in such an assessment.
It is further stipulated that acquisition of land cannot be done unless such assessment has been completed.

However, Section 10(A) empowers the State Government to exempt certain projects, from the application of the provisions to Section 4 to section 10 of the Act (Section 4 to Section 10 are contained in Chapter-II and Chapter-III of the Act).

After conduct of such assessment, a preliminary notification, under section 11, would have to be issued by the appropriate government, setting out the lands that are sought to be acquired and the public purpose for which the acquisition is proposed.
This notification is to be given vide publicity by way of a procedure and requirements set out in Section 11 itself.

After completion of the procedures set out in Section 11 to section 18, the appropriate government has to issue a declaration, under section 19,
along with a summary on rehabilitation and resettlement, after which steps for passing RRR,J & Dr.
KMR,J of an award, vesting of the land, payment of compensation etc., can be completed.
20. The above scheme of the Act shows that a notification under Section 11, and the declaration under Section 19 has to be given by the appropriate government'.
The exemption, from the application of section 4 to 9, is to be given, under Section 10(A), by the State Government.
The term appropriate government' has been defined under Section 3(e), as set out above.

This definition limits the expression appropriate government' to either the State Government or the Central Government, depending upon the acquisition of the land and the purpose for which the land is being P. 7 acquired.

entities.text: P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After defining the term appropriate government' in this manner, a proviso has been inserted to enable the appropriate government (either State or Central) to delegate the functions of the appropriate government to the Collector of the District.
This delegation is to be done by way of a notification and by fixing the outer limit of the area that can be acquired by the Collector of the District, acting as the appropriate government.
Section 10(A) empowers the State Government to exempt projects, from the application of the provisions of Section 4 to 10. RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J 21.

In the present case the notification under Section 11, the declaration under Section 19 and the exemption, from the application of section 4 to 9, under Section 10A, was issued by the District Collector.

22. On the question of the grant of exemption, under section 10A, the learned Advocate General would also rely upon G.O.Ms.No.16, dated 29.01.2025, issued by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, under Section 10A, as introduced by Ordinance No.9 of 2014.
In this notification, all the projects, set out in Section 10A were exempted from the provisions of Section 4 to 10 of the Act.

23. The issue of whether the District Collector, in the absence of a notification, under the proviso to Section 3(e) of the Act, can act as the appropriate government, came up before a Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.32956 of 2015.

The Division Bench, in its judgment, dated 04.11.2022, decided this issue in the following manner:
44. Section 3(e) of the LA Act, 2013 defines the word appropriate government' to mean, in relation to acquisition of land situated within the territory of, State, the State Government with proviso that in respect of a public purpose in a District for an area not exceeding such as may be notified by the appropriate government, the Collector of such District shall be deemed to be the appropriate Government.

In view of the above definition, petitioners have contended that in the absence of a specific notification by the appropriate Government, i.e. the State Government determining the area for which the District Collector shall be deemed to be the appropriate Government, delegating the power to the District RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J Collector without specifying the limit is illegal and does not satisfy the requirement of law.
46. Admittedly, the State Government has notified the respective District Collectors to be the appropriate Government for the acquisition of lands under the statutory rules.
Rule 2(b) thereof has authorized the District Collector to perform the duties and functions of the appropriate Government for any extent of land.

The issue is whether a separate notification is required as is mentioned in the proviso to Section 3(e) or the delegation of powers of the appropriate Government to the District Collector under the Rules, 2014, would be sufficient compliance of the proviso to Section 3(e) of the LA Act, 2013, which are statutory Rules made in exercise of powers under Section 109 of the LA Act,
2013.

The same has been issued after compliance with the pre- condition of prior publication as required under Section 112 of P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49712520/
8 45. W.P.No.8639 of 2016 and the LA Act, 2013.

entities.text: P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sub-section (1) of Section 109 provides that subject to the other provisions of the Act, appropriate Government may, by notification make Rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

If the provision contained under the proviso to Section 3(e) is read in harmony with Section 109(1) and Section 112 of the LA Act, 2013, it can be safely concluded that there is no requirement of a separate notification delegating powers of appropriate Government to the Collector of a District in respect of a particular area.

If the Rules themselves which have already been notified enable the District Collector to function as appropriate Government for any extent of land within his District, the same cannot be faulted with in the absence of a separate notification.
IN our considered view, Rule 2(b) of the Rules, 2014, is in compliance with the proviso to Section 3(e) of the LA Act, 2013 and, as such, there is no violation of the said provision.

Accordingly, this argument of the petitioners fails and rejected.
24.
Only the State Government or the Central Government would be the appropriate Government under Section 3(e).
The District Collector would also come within the deeming fiction of being the appropriate government when a notification is issued by the appropriate RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J government.
Such notification would also have to stipulate the extent of area, within the District, for which the district collector can act as the appropriate government.

The Division Bench in W.P.No.
32956 of 2015, had taken the view that the definition of appropriate government' under Rule 3(b)
was sufficient to invoke the legal fiction of the District Collector being the appropriate government.

The Division Bench also took the view that the publication of the Rules, by way of notification, meets the requirement of notification, under the proviso to section 3 (e).
25.
With due respect, we are unable to agree with the aforesaid exposition of law.

26. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Dinesh and Ors Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors, had analyzed Section 3 (e) in the following manner:
20.

entities.text: Dinesh and Ors Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Collector would be deemed to be the appropriate Government' under the proviso to Section 3 (e) of the Act of 2013 only when a land acquisition notification is issued by the appropriate Government that is the State Government indicating the limits of the area to be acquired for a public purpose and appointing the Collector as the authority empowered to acquire that particular area of land in the district' over which the officer holds jurisdiction.

Hence, this proviso requires notification by the State Government of a particular area within the district to be acquired for public purpose and only for such limited area, RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J the Collector would be authorized by deeming fiction to act as the appropriate Government.
27. We are in respectful agreement with the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
In the present case, Rule 2 (b) stipulates that the term appropriate government, would include the district collector for any extent of land.

Even if publication of Rules is to be treated as a notification, it would be a general notification, delegating power to the district collector, without any limit on the extent of area for which the district collector can act as the appropriate government.

The requirement of the proviso to section 3 (e), as interpreted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, is that a separate notification P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49712520/
9 has to be issued, for each acquisition proceeding, after the extent of area, for which the Collector can act as the appropriate government, is fixed.

entities.text: P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the subsequent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the view of the division bench, in W.P. No. 32956 of 2015, that Rule 2 (b) is the notification, for the purposes of the proviso to section 3 (e), may not be good law anymore.

28. The learned single judge had taken the view that the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
cited above would not be applicable, in the State of Andhra Pradesh, because there was no provision,
akin to Rule 2 (b), in the Madhya Pradesh rules.

The learned Advocate General had also taken us through the Madhya Pradesh Rules RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J to show that a Rule similar to Rule 2 (b)
was not available in the Madhya Pradesh Rules.
This view, with respect does not appear to be correct.

Rule 2 which contains the definitions, starts with the following words:
2. Definitions: (1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires:
The above language makes it clear that the definition in Rule 2 (b) is restricted to the Rules and cannot be extended to the provisions of the Act.
The view of the earlier division bench, that this definition, which should be confined to the rules, can be extended to the provisions of the Act, requires to be reconsidered.
29. Apart from the above, the Act requires a notification to be issued, to include the Collector within the definition of appropriate government'.
The term notification is defined, in Section 3(v) of the Act, to be a notification published in the Gazette of India or the State Gazette.
As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the above judgment, separate notifications have to be issued.

The notification of the Rules would not, incidentally, amount to a notification required under the proviso to section 3 (e).
30.
There is another aspect that needs to be considered.
The Rules have used the term District Collector as well as the term RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J appropriate government in an interchangeable manner.
There would be situations where, within the same Rule, the District Collector, would have to function in the dual capacity of District Collector and appropriate government.
Rule 11 and 16 are such instances.
Rule 2 (b) appears to have been brought in to cover such situations.
This interpretation may lead to the conclusion that such a definition cannot be stretched to treat it as a notification for the purposes of the proviso to section 3 (e) .

31. Another facet of the appeal is the ground that the district collector cannot issue an exemption,
under section 10A of the Act.
The learned Advocate General has submitted that, by virtue of rule 2 (b), the District Collector would be the appropriate government and can issue such exemptions.
32. The view of this Court, that the definition contained in the rules would not be applicable to the provisions of the Act would apply here.
Further, the government, referred to in Section 10A is the State Government and not the appropriate government.

This has significance, as Rule 2 (i)
defines State Government to mean the Government of Andhra Pradesh.

In view of a separate definition, given to the term State Government, the inclusion of District Collector in Rule 2 P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49712520/
10 (b) would not extend to treating the District Collector as the State Government.
RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J 33.

The discussion, relating to the power of the District Collector to grant exemption, under Section 10A, is rendered academic, by virtue of G.O.Ms.No.16, dated 29.01.2025, issued by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, under Section 10(A), as introduced by Ordinance No.9 of 2014.
In this notification, all the projects, set out in Section 10(A) were exempted from the provisions of Section 4 to 10 of the Act.
Section 10 (A), was introduced, by Ordinance No. 9 of 2014, and the said section was available when G.O.Ms. No. 16 had been issued.
Subsequently, the Ordinance lapsed, without being replaced by an Act.
Later, the provision was reintroduced by virtue of Amendment Act No. 22 of 2018, with retrospective effect from 01.01.2014.

By virtue of the retrospective effect of the amendment, the exemption granted, under G.O.Ms.No.16, would continue to hold the field, and the validity, or otherwise, of the exemption granted by the District Collector would not be determinative of the exemption.
34. As any deviation from the interpretation, given by the earlier division bench, could result in widespread dislocation of the existing acquisition processes.

It would also be appropriate that there is an authoritative pronouncement, on the question of whether the interpretation of the above provisions, by the earlier division bench RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J requires to reconsidered.

This court,
for these reasons, deems it appropriate to refer the matter to a full bench for an authoritative pronouncement on the question of whether the inclusion of the District Collector, in the definition of Appropriate government, in Rule 2 (b) can be treated as a notification under the proviso to section 3 (e), empowering the District Collector to discharge the functions of the appropriate government.
35. The learned Advocate General has contended that, an investment of Rupees Ten Thousand crores, is being delayed, on account of the stay granted by this court.
He has also submitted that delay in grounding the project would postpone the employment opportunities that would accrue to the unemployed in the area.
We would need to balance this fact with the requirement of law.
As far as the question of the effect of the interim order, of the learned Single Judge, of the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh, dated 28.02.2008, in W.P.No.4159 of 2008, is concerned
, the same can not give way to permit acquisition in the face of the orders of the Court.

However, the question of the jurisdiction of the District Collector which was earlier decided in favour of the State, has now been reopened, on account of the subsequent view of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and also in view of the doubt entertained by us, whether such interpretation was correct.
In such circumstances, it would be RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J necessary to balance the requirements of public interest and the rights of the appellant.
The extent of the land of the appellant is Acres 4.49 cents.
It would not be equitable to hold up a project of the size mentioned by the learned Advocate General, till the rights of the Appellant are decided.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
A learned Single Judge of the erstwhile High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh, had granted status quo existing on the day of the order to be maintained.
While there is no dispute that writ petitions filed against the same acquisition process had been disposed of, the fact remains that the present Writ Petition has not been disposed of and the order of the learned Single Judge continues to hold the field.
17. The State, instead of getting the said writ petition closed, on the ground that the notification under challenge had lapsed, has chosen to take the stand that the said order of status quo does not preclude further acquisition process.
Though the order of the learned Single Judge was passed in the context of the acquisition process, initiated under the notification, dated 21.03.2006, the same would enure to the benefit of the petitioner, in relation to any further acquisition of the land, for the same purpose.
If the provision contained under the proviso to Section 3(e) is read in harmony with Section 109(1) and Section 112 of the LA Act, 2013, it can be safely concluded that there is no requirement of a separate notification delegating powers of appropriate Government to the Collector of a District in respect of a particular area.
If the Rules themselves which have already been notified enable the District Collector to function as appropriate Government for any extent of land within his District, the same cannot be faulted with in the absence of a separate notification.
IN our considered view, Rule 2(b) of the Rules, 2014, is in compliance with the proviso to Section 3(e) of the LA Act, 2013 and, as such, there is no violation of the said provision.
Only the State Government or the Central Government would be the appropriate Government under Section 3(e).
The District Collector would also come within the deeming fiction of being the appropriate government when a notification is issued by the appropriate RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J government.
The Collector would be deemed to be the appropriate Government' under the proviso to Section 3 (e) of the Act of 2013 only when a land acquisition notification is issued by the appropriate Government that is the State Government indicating the limits of the area to be acquired for a public purpose and appointing the Collector as the authority empowered to acquire that particular area of land in the district' over which the officer holds jurisdiction.
Hence, this proviso requires notification by the State Government of a particular area within the district to be acquired for public purpose and only for such limited area, RRR,J & Dr. KMR,J the Collector would be authorized by deeming fiction to act as the appropriate Government.
In the present case, Rule 2 (b) stipulates that the term appropriate government, would include the district collector for any extent of land.
Even if publication of Rules is to be treated as a notification, it would be a general notification, delegating power to the district collector, without any limit on the extent of area for which the district collector can act as the appropriate government.
The requirement of the proviso to section 3 (e), as interpreted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, is that a separate notification P. Rathnaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49712520/

By virtue of the retrospective effect of the amendment, the exemption granted, under G.O.Ms.No.16, would continue to hold the field, and the validity, or otherwise, of the exemption granted by the District Collector would not be determinative of the exemption.
This court,
for these reasons, deems it appropriate to refer the matter to a full bench for an authoritative pronouncement on the question of whether the inclusion of the District Collector, in the definition of Appropriate government, in Rule 2 (b) can be treated as a notification under the proviso to section 3 (e), empowering the District Collector to discharge the functions of the appropriate government.
